description: Moon & Mars StoryLab explores NASA’s abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars through science storytelling. Our project, “The Moon Has a Heartbeat?”, focuses on the Apollo 11 seismometer and how it helped scientists study moonquakes and the Moon’s interior. We aim to create an engaging, illustrated learning experience that inspires young readers through scientific evidence, curiosity, and creative storytelling.
summary:
What if the Moon had a heartbeat? This simple question became the beginning of my journey.

**“The Moon Has a Heartbeat?”** is a 21-page illustrated educational science story I created as part of the Moon & Mars StoryLab challenge. It follows a curious child whose question leads to the fascinating world of lunar science.

Through this story, I explore the historic Apollo 11 mission, the Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE), different types of moonquakes, and the hidden structure of the Moon. I combined scientific research, NASA-related resources, storytelling, illustrations, and scientific diagrams to make these complex ideas easier and more enjoyable for young readers.

My goal is not just to share scientific facts, but to awaken curiosity in children and encourage them to ask questions about the universe. I believe that every great discovery begins with a little curiosity.

This project is especially meaningful to me because it shows how a simple question can open the door to a much bigger journey of exploration.

**Explore Yourself. Explore the World.**
details:
I developed “The Moon Has a Heartbeat?”, a 21-page illustrated educational science story designed to introduce young readers to lunar science through imagination and storytelling.

The story begins with a child's curiosity about whether the Moon has a heartbeat. This question leads to an exploration of the Apollo 11 mission, the Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE), different types of moonquakes, and the Moon's internal structure.

I used scientific research, NASA resources, illustrations, and diagrams to explain these topics in simple, engaging language. I prepared the story and its accompanying six-slide presentation using Google Docs and Google Slides.

The main benefit of this project is that it makes space science more approachable for children. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity, scientific thinking, and an interest in space exploration.

The creative element is the storytelling approach: instead of presenting scientific facts as a list, I connect them through a child's imaginative question and a journey of discovery.
